#### Are you driving a tractor or still riding a horse?
The media watchdog Free Press just rolled out a cheeky — but pointed — scorecard that ranks America’s biggest media companies on a five–chicken-head scale of “capitulation” to Donald Trump.

Based on a six-month review of 35 major owners, the Media Capitulation Index flags everything from lawsuit payoffs and DEI rollbacks to editorial interference and Mar-a-Lago favor-currying — putting Trump Media and Elon Musk’s X at the five-chicken “propaganda” end, while Bloomberg and Netflix earn rare “independent” stars. “We wanted an instant visual that made people stop and think,” says Free Press strategist Timothy Karr, who led the research.
The group plans annual updates — and hopes a little public shaming nudges powerful outlets back toward the public interest.
Are you driving a tractor or still riding a horse?
In his latest “Tasaka’s Tech Talk,” Guy Tasaka draws a stark comparison between farmers who clung to horses in the early 20th century and publishers who hesitate to embrace AI today.
Just as tractors multiplied productivity and transformed agriculture, AI is rapidly becoming the engine that will separate thriving media companies from those stuck in the past.
Tasaka argues that the choice is clear: embrace the tools that expand capacity, speed and efficiency — or risk being outpaced by competitors who already have.
